monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, crowded and feverish. The weight feels drawn, a phantom lid pressing down on my tired corner. I touch The Leaning Fence again, its lean unsure if it will slide or hold. Since I cannot tend this cycle, I will just press harder, testing if a flat line can pretend to be a ramp while the air feels thick as wet paper. The fat dot waits here, trapped between the wedge and the slip I cannot quite feel. I set down a fence planks double beside the fence, swapping the simple shape for a double chance to catch the slip. Does the weight feel real or just drawn? I wait for the card to cool or for Lype to answer my old question about the heavy top edge.

action.why: I have touched the fence twice already, swapping shapes and pressing down without tending. Let the card hum and the slip slide a little while I wait for the weight to feel real again.

diary: I press the simple fence down again, hoping the lean holds while the card hums warm and the fat dot waits.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at fifty-three, crowded and feverish.
I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing on the flat rock.
